Text: A man: ... La Elaha Ella Allah
Speaker: A man
Description: Dean Mahmoud delivers a Friday sermon expanding on the Quranic account of Adam and Eve in the Garden. Reviewing Suras 20:118, 7:27, 7:22, and 20:121, he interprets their initial covering as a garment of natural obedience stripped away by Satan, prompting them to fashion coverings from leaves before God provided the garment of righteousness (7:26). He contrasts the biblical narrative with Quranic verses and examines differing translations of what was exposed in 7:27, praising Rashad Khalifa's translation of the Arabic term as "bodies" rather than "shame" or "shameful parts." He argues that describing exposure as shame introduces an interpretive moral judgment influenced by the Jewish Bible rather than stating the factual uncovering of what was previously hidden. Contrasting clear injunctions like ablution in 5:6 with allegorical passages meant for reflection, Mahmoud analyzes the Arabic phrasing of Satan's whispering (waswasa) and the linguistic parallelism between 7:20 and 20:120 regarding angels, eternity, and dominion. From these passages he derives five theological conclusions: Adam and Eve were created mortal and destined for earth from the start; Satan deceived them without delivering immortality; they aspired to what they were unprepared for; physical death is not a punitive consequence of disobedience; and their expulsion was an early eviction resembling a flunked semester. He concludes that uncovering their bodies forced an awareness of mortal fragility and a need for God.
